1.w: “Indeed, my eyes have seen all this; my ears have heard and understood it.

2.w: What you know, I know also; I am not inferior to you!

3.w: But I wish to speak to the Almighty, and I desire to argue my case with God.

4.w: But you, however, are inventors of lies; all of you are worthless physicians!

5.w: If only you would keep completely silent! For you, that would be wisdom.

6.w: Listen now to my argument, and be attentive to my lips’ contentions.

7.w: Will you speak wickedly on God’s behalf? Will you speak deceitfully for him?

8.w: Will you show him partiality? Will you argue the case for God?

9.w: Would it turn out well if he would examine you? Or as one deceives a man would you deceive him?

10.w: He would certainly rebuke you if you secretly showed partiality.

11.w: Would not his splendor terrify you and the fear he inspires fall on you?

12.w: Your maxims are proverbs of ashes; your defenses are defenses of clay.

13.w: “Refrain from talking with me so that I may speak; then let come to me what may.

14.w: Why do I put myself in peril, and take my life in my hands?

15.w: Even if he slays me, I will hope in him; I will surely defend my ways to his face.

16.w: Moreover, this will become my deliverance, for no godless person would come before him.

17.w: Listen carefully to my words; let your ears be attentive to my explanation.

18.w: See now, I have prepared my case; I know that I am right.

19.w: Who will contend with me? If anyone can, I will be silent and die.

20.w: Only in two things spare me, O God, and then I will not hide from your face:

21.w: Remove your hand far from me and stop making me afraid with your terror.

22.w: Then call, and I will answer, or I will speak, and you respond to me.

23.w: How many are my iniquities and sins? Show me my transgression and my sin.

24.w: Why do you hide your face and regard me as your enemy?

25.w: Do you wish to torment a windblown leaf and chase after dry chaff?

26.w: For you write down bitter things against me and cause me to inherit the sins of my youth.

27.w: And you put my feet in the stocks and you watch all my movements; you put marks on the soles of my feet.

28.w: So I waste away like something rotten, like a garment eaten by moths.
